gaps.sentence: Don't leave ___ any details in your report.
The plane takes ___ in ten minutes.
gaps.explanation: take off = leave the ground (plane); also remove clothes; become successful (career took off).

gaps.sentence: The new manager wants to back ___ the sales team's proposal.
gaps.explanation: back up = support (a person, plan); also make a copy of data.

gaps.sentence: If you don't know the word, look it ___ in a dictionary.
gaps.explanation: look a word up = find it in a dictionary/reference.

gaps.sentence: He ___ up the word in an online dictionary.
gaps.explanation: 'Look a word up' = check its meaning.

gaps.sentence: She waited at the restaurant for an hour, but he had stood her ___ again.
gaps.explanation: 'Stand somebody up' = fail to keep an arranged meeting.

gaps.sentence: She's taken ___ knitting to relax after work.
gaps.explanation: take up = start (a hobby, sport, activity).

gaps.sentence: The new stadium made ___ an impressive sight.
gaps.explanation: make for = produce a particular result (make for a good atmosphere); also move towards.
